_comment: The words of Part D's steps in play (game/story/deeds.py say(); their one-line fallbacks are deeds.DEFAULT_WORDS): asking someone to stand with you, raising a town, confronting a traitor, setting out with someone in your care, a night to be held, a rite, a captive who talks, an ambush, a band waiting. {villain}, {villain_short}, {town}, {home} as in every tale; {who}, {place}, {night}, {to} where the step gives them.

recruit_ask: Will you stand with us against {villain}?
I can't do this alone. Will you come?
When we go against {villain_short}, I want you beside me.
recruit_yes: "Yes. Yes, I will. Somebody has to."
"I've been waiting for someone to ask me that." A hand, rough and hard. "I'm with you."
"I'll come. Don't thank me. Just don't make me sorry."
recruit_no: "Not yet. Ask me again when I have slept on it."
"I have children. Give me a day to think of them, and then ask me again."
"No. Not today." They will not look at you. "Maybe tomorrow."
rally_ask: Call your people together. {villain_short} will not be stopped by one blade.
Every one of {town} who can hold a spear. That is what it will take.
You can stand behind your doors and wait, or you can stand with me.
rally_yes: "Every one who can hold a spear will be there. You have my word."
The bell rings, and they come: farmers, smiths, the miller's sons, old soldiers with rust on their helmets. Not many. Enough.
"We've been afraid long enough," someone at the back says, and they all start talking at once.
rally_no: "They are frightened. Give me a day, and ask me again."
Nobody steps forward. Nobody looks at you. "Tomorrow," the headman says. "Ask tomorrow."
"Fight? With what? Come back when they've had time to think on it."
confront_ask: I know what you have done, {who}.
I know who you talk to at night, {who}.
confront_yield: "...All right. All right. I'll tell you everything. Just keep them off me."
The colour goes out of their face. "They said they'd burn my house with my children in it," they whisper. "What was I to do?"
For a long moment nothing. Then they sit down, very suddenly, as if their legs had been cut. "Ask, then."
confront_fight: "You should have kept your mouth shut." There are men behind you now.
"Clever," they say, and whistle, and the door behind you opens.
They do not answer. They step back, and the men who were drinking in the corner stand up.
escort_ask: We set out now, for {to}. Are you ready?
The road to {to}. Stay close to me, and we'll get there.
If we're going to {to}, it's now or not at all.
escort_set_out: "I'm ready. Let's not stop until we're there."
"Gods keep us," they mutter, and take up the reins.
"I'll go where you go. Just don't leave me on the road."
hold_set: They will come to {place} on the night of {night}. Be there.
On the night of {night}, at {place}. That is when it will be decided.
{place}, the night of {night}. Whatever is coming, it is coming then.
hold_wave: They come again, out of the dark, before you have caught your breath.
No rest. Another line of them comes up out of the night.
You have hardly wiped your blade before the next of them are on you.
hold_won: The last of them falls back into the dark, and the night is quiet. {place} still stands.
Dawn comes grey over {place}, and nothing is left standing but you and yours.
It is over. You held {place}. Somebody starts to laugh, and cannot stop.
hold_lost: You fall back from {place}, and it is theirs.
There were too many. {place} is lost.
hold_missed: You were not at {place} on the night they came.
The night came and went at {place}, and you were somewhere else.
They came to {place} that night, and nobody stood in their way.
rite_done: It is done. The air itself seems to lighten.
The last word goes out of you, and something that was holding its breath lets it go.
It is finished. The cold goes out of the stones.
rite_fail: The words will not come right. You will have to try again tomorrow.
Something stops your tongue. Not today.
It does not take. Rest, and come back to it.
rite_needs: You do not have what the rite needs.
Not yet: the rite needs what you have not found.
Without what binds it, the words are only words.
captive_talks: {who} talks, as the taken often do, and it is worth hearing.
{who} holds out longer than you would think, and then tells you everything.
{who} spits, and swears, and then talks fast, as if the words were burning.
ambush: They were waiting for you on the road, as if they knew you would come this way.
Out of the ditch, out of the trees, all at once: an ambush, and a good one.
A rope comes up across the road, and then they are everywhere.
band_here: There they are: {who}, and they have seen you.
